name: Subsequent 37
popularity: Moog's two-note paraphonic analog keyboard synth (successor to the Sub 37); the manual says every knob and button transmits MIDI, which suits DAW automation. Source: Subsequent 37 manual p.11.
noteRangeNote: Manual spec page: 'Guaranteed note range at 8' of Note 18 to 116'. This is the calibrated pitch range, not a statement about which MIDI note numbers are accepted.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Per preset: PRESET EDIT MENU 2.2 BEND UP (+0..+24) and 2.3 BEND DOWN (-0..-24). Also CC 107 (bend up 0..24) and CC 108 (bend down 0..24). Manual p.42 and p.55.

controls.label: LFO RATE

controls.label: FILTER AMT
controls.notes: 14-bit pair: CC 11 is MSB (0-127); CC 43 is LSB, giving 0-16383 with both. Manual p.53. Amount of Mod 1 source applied to filter cutoff.

controls.notes: 14-bit pair: CC 20 is MSB (0-127); CC 52 is LSB, giving 0-16383 with both. Manual p.53. Mod 1 amount to the selected destination (MOD 1 DEST).

setup: Press MIDI, go to MIDI MENU 1.1 IN CHANNEL and set the channel the app sends on (default 1; ALL = omni).
MIDI MENU 2.1 IN PORTS: set to BOTH (default) or to the port you use (DIN or USB).
MIDI MENU 1.4 RCV PGM CHG: ON (default) if the app sends program changes.
No setting is needed to receive CCs. MIDI MENU 3.3 OUT FILTERS > KNB NRPN/CC and CC FORMAT only change what the synth transmits.
notes: All main-sound knobs are reachable by CC, so no NRPN is used here. The manual's NRPN chart (p.56-59) is unusable as printed: several value-range cells are shifted by one row (for example 'OSC 2 FREQUENCY 3', 'OSC 1 LEVEL 2') and the table stops at NRPN 524 before the amp envelope. NRPN fields are left null on purpose. The manual does not state whether to send the 14-bit MSB or LSB first; MIDI convention is MSB then LSB.

name: Grandmother
popularity: Moog's semi-modular analog keyboard with spring reverb and arp/sequencer, aimed at hands-on patching. Source: Grandmother manual specs p.54.
noteRangeNote: The manual does not state which MIDI note numbers are accepted. Keyboard is 32 keys.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Global setting: hold HOLD + Osc 1 SYNC until SYNC blinks, press the D#1 key, then press one of the lowest 12 white keys (F0..C2) for 1..12 semitones (p.38). Over MIDI: CC 107 (up) and CC 108 (down) use the value table on p.44 (0..24 semitones, e.g. 2 semitones = 10, 12 = 61, 24 = 123). Manual also lists RPN 0 Pitch Bend Amount.

respondsToNotes: CC 7 is not in the chart. Grandmother has no presets, so program change does nothing. Velocity is received but not wired to anything inside; it only appears at the KB VEL OUT patch jack (spec p.54). CC 64 sustain is listed under Additional MIDI Functions.

controls.label: RATE
controls.notes: Chart: 'MODULATION RATE CC 3, 0-127 (or 0-16383 using CC3 & CC 35)'. Manual p.43.

controls.label: GLIDE
controls.notes: Chart: 'GLIDE TIME CC 5 (or 14-bit with CC 37)'. Glide on/off is CC 65.

controls.label: GLIDE ON/OFF
controls.notes: Chart p.43: 0 = Off, 64 = On. There is no separate panel button; this is a MIDI-side switch.

controls.label: FREQUENCY
controls.notes: Chart: 'OSCILLATOR 2 FREQUENCY CC 12 (or 14-bit with CC 44)'. Detunes osc 2 +/-7 semitones; center = unison (p.12).

controls.label: OCTAVE
controls.notes: Chart p.43 values 0/32/64/96; in-between ranges inferred.

controls.label: OCTAVE
controls.notes: Chart p.43 prints 32'/16'/8'/4' for both oscillators, but the Oscillator 2 text (p.12) says its switch is 16'/8'/4'/2'. Treat the footage names as uncertain; the 4 value positions are what the chart gives.

controls.label: SYNC
controls.notes: Chart: 'OSCILLATOR 2 SYNC CC 77, 0 = Off, 64 = On'.

uncontrollable: Not reachable by MIDI at all (the chart has no entry): filter CUTOFF, RESONANCE, envelope ATTACK/DECAY/SUSTAIN/RELEASE, mixer levels, noise, oscillator wave knobs, PITCH AMT / CUTOFF AMT / PULSE WIDTH AMT, spring REVERB MIX, VCA volume. On Grandmother these knobs are analog and must be turned by hand (or moved via patch-cable CV).
setup: Set the MIDI channel: hold HOLD (left-hand controller) and SYNC (Oscillator 1) until SYNC blinks, press the F#0 key, then press one of the first 16 white keys (F0..G2) for channel 1..16. Press SYNC to exit. Default is channel 1.
No other setting is needed to receive the CCs listed.
notes: Very few knobs are CC-controllable: only modulation RATE, GLIDE time and Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY are continuous; the rest are switches. A Moog forum thread reports CC 103 (Gated Glide), 107/108 (bend amount) and 119 (transpose) misbehaving on some firmware; not verified here.

setup: Press GLOBAL. Use the parameter and value knobs.
3. MIDI Channel: set to the app's channel (or All).
7. MIDI Param Receive: set to NRPN for full resolution, or CC for the CC numbers above. The synth listens to only one of these at a time.
8. MIDI Control Enable: On (needed for mod wheel, pedal, volume).
9. MIDI Program Enable: On if the app sends program changes.
NRPN messages: CC 99 = param MSB, CC 98 = param LSB, CC 6 = value MSB, CC 38 = value LSB. Split the number into two 7-bit halves (e.g. 156 = MSB 1, LSB 28).
notes: All NRPNs above are Layer A. Layer B is the Layer A number + 2048 (table p.90-94). CCs only reach Layer A as documented.

name: Take 5
popularity: Sequential's compact 5-voice analog poly with 44 keys, a lower-cost Prophet-style synth. Source: Take 5 User's Guide p.1.
noteRangeNote: MIDI implementation: 'Note number 0-127'. Keyboard is 44 keys.
defaultChannelNote: Guide lists 'All, 1...16'; factory default not stated.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Per program: press PROGRAM, find Pitch Bend Up (0..12) and Pitch Bend Down (0..24), write the program (User's Guide printed p.54). MIDI: CC 85 / NRPN 75 (up 0-12), CC 86 / NRPN 76 (down 0-24). Default not stated.

respondsToNotes: CC 7 is in the CC table as 'Master Volume' (needs Param Receive = CC); the 'Received Controller Messages' list omits it, but 'MIDI Control On' says the synth responds to volume. Program change selects programs 1-16 of the selected bank; needs 'MIDI Program Receive' On. Damper CC 64: any non-zero value is on.

name: DeepMind 12
popularity: Behringer's 12-voice analog poly with 4 FX engines, sold at a low price for its voice count. Source: DeepMind 12 User Manual cover.
noteRangeNote: MIDI chart says 'Note numbers C0-C8' without saying which octave-numbering convention, so a MIDI number range is not given.
defaultChannelNote: Manual describes RX-CHANNEL 1-16 but does not state the default.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Per program: POLY EDIT page 2, P.BEND RANGE+ and P.BEND RANGE- (0..24, default 2) (manual p.67). NRPN 36 (up) and 37 (down), 0-24.

respondsToNotes: CC chart marks CC 7 'Channel Volume' as recognized; it does not say this moves the panel VOLUME knob. Program change needs PROG-CHANGE set to RX or RX-TX.

controls.label: PITCH MOD
controls.notes: Pitch mod depth; source chosen in OSC edit (NRPN 22).

controls.label: SQUAREWAVE
controls.notes: No CC.

controls.label: SAWTOOTH
controls.notes: No CC.

controls.label: PITCH
controls.notes: Base pitch of osc 2.

controls.label: LFO
controls.notes: LFO depth to cutoff; which LFO is NRPN 46.

controls.label: 2-POLE
controls.notes: No CC.

controls.label: INVERT
controls.notes: NRPN name 'VCF Envelope Polarity'. No CC.

controls.label: BOOST
controls.notes: NRPN name 'VCF Bass Boost'. No CC.

controls.label: A
controls.notes: The A/D/S/R faders are shared; the VCA/VCF/MOD buttons pick which envelope they edit. Each envelope stage has its own CC/NRPN.

controls.label: S
controls.notes: CC left null: the chart prints CC 44 as 'VCA Envelope Sustain', a duplicate of CC 40. It is very likely a misprint for VCF Envelope Sustain (it sits between VCF Decay 43 and VCF Release 45) but the document does not say so. Test CC 44 on hardware before using it. NRPN 64 is unambiguous.

controls.label: VCA Envelope Depth
controls.notes: Edit-menu parameter. No CC.

controls.label: PORTAMENTO
controls.notes: CC 5 is listed as 'Portamento Time'.

controls.label: VOLUME
controls.notes: CC 7 'Channel Volume' is recognized; the manual does not say it is the same as the panel VOLUME knob.

effectsNote: Effects are 4 slots with 12 parameters each whose meaning depends on the effect type, so there is no fixed delay-time or reverb-mix number. CCs: slot 1 params 1-12 = CC 62, 63, 65-74; slot 2 params 1-12 = CC 75-86; slot 3 params 1-9 = CC 87-95 and 10-12 = CC 102-104; slot 4 params have no CC. Slot types CC 105-108; slot gains CC 109-112; FX mode CC 114. NRPN: FX 1-4 type 166/179/192/205 (0-33), FX 1 params 167-178, FX 2 180-191, FX 3 193-204, FX 4 206-217 (0-255).
setup: Press GLOBAL, open CONNECTIVITY.
For 5-pin MIDI: open MIDI SETTINGS, set RX-CHANNEL to the app's channel.
For USB: open USB SETTINGS, set RX-CHANNEL to the app's channel.
Set PROG-CHANGE to RX or RX-TX if the app sends program changes.
No receive mode switch is needed: the manual says CC and NRPN are always received. MIDI-CTRL / USB-CTRL only change what is transmitted.
NRPN messages: CC 99 = param MSB, CC 98 = param LSB, CC 6 = value MSB, CC 38 = value LSB. The synth tracks the selected NRPN separately for USB, Wi-Fi and 5-pin MIDI.
notes: The CC chart is dated 'Version 1.0, 01 September 2016'. Later firmware may differ; not checked. Chart also has a duplicate 'VCA Envelope Sustain Curve' at CC 52 and 56 (curves, not used here).

name: Model D
popularity: Low-cost analog clone of the Minimoog Model D in Eurorack format with MIDI and USB. Source: Model D User Manual cover.
noteRangeNote: Not stated. 'MIDI Note Zero Volts' SysEx setting (default 36) sets which MIDI note gives 0 V pitch CV.
defaultChannelNote: Set by the four rear-panel MIDI CHANNEL DIP switches (or SysEx 0x0A/00, default 0 = channel 1 when switches are disabled).

bendRangeSemitones.how: SysEx only: F0 00 20 32 00 <device id> 0A 03 00 <0..12> F7 (Command Table p.30, default 12). Send with a SysEx tool over USB.

respondsToNotes: The manual names no CC numbers at all. It says the MOD DEPTH can also be set with the modulation wheel of a MIDI keyboard. No presets (so no program change), no velocity routing, no sustain or volume CC mentioned.

controls.label: MOD DEPTH (via MIDI mod wheel)
controls.notes: The manual (p.8 and p.13) says the mod wheel of a MIDI keyboard adjusts modulation depth. It does not print the CC number; CC 1 is the MIDI standard's mod wheel controller. Response curve is set by SysEx 0x0A/0B (Soft default, Med, Hard). The physical MOD DEPTH knob does not move.

uncontrollable: Every panel knob (oscillators, mixer, filter cutoff/emphasis/contour, envelopes, glide, LFO rate, volume) is analog and has no CC or NRPN. Only notes, pitch bend and mod wheel are received, plus SysEx for global settings.
setup: Set the rear-panel MIDI CHANNEL DIP switches to the app's channel (table on the rear-panel page of the manual).
Optional: to change bend range, mod wheel curve, key priority or transpose, send the SysEx strings in the Command Table (p.30) from a SysEx tool over USB.
notes: Effectively no knob can be moved over MIDI. Rules for this synth can only play notes, bend pitch and use the mod wheel.

sources.what: Mirror of the Behringer MODEL D User Manual: p.8 controllers section (mod wheel), p.11 rear panel MIDI channel switches, p.13 special modes, p.30 SysEx command table
